## Claims
- [source-backed] Original Conjecture 4.10 states that both Theorem 4.8 families are minimal: the right-adjoined family \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\) and the lower-adjoined family \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\), for \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\). [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 864-876; lines 938-946]
- [source-backed] The 2024 paper’s Theorem 1.2 proves minimality only for the lower-adjoined family \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\), for bigrassmannian \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), in \(H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 219-235]
- [source-backed] Its Corollary 4.6 again concludes minimality only for that lower-adjoined family. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 827-832]
- [source-backed] The right-adjoined family is addressed only in Remark 4.7: it is identified as the conjugate family, and the paper says one “could straightforwardly” transpose the arguments to prove its minimality; no transposed theorem or corollary is stated there. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 833-840]

## Strategy
Compared the original two-clause conjecture with the theorem, corollary, and remark in the later proof paper.

The requested bibliographic classification is established: source-relatively, the 2024 text proves the lower-adjoined clause, while it presents the right-adjoined clause as a stated transposition route rather than a separately executed theorem-level proof. This classification is separate from any accepted project proof of both clauses.

## Gaps
Bounded negative result: among the inspected full texts, no source was found that explicitly states and proves the right-adjoined clause as a theorem/corollary.
